blueprints.name: Morrow Lab
blueprints.tagline: Explore system behavior through reproducible experiments.
blueprints.purpose: A compact simulation workbench for running seeded thermal-system experiments, adjusting assumptions, comparing response traces and preserving experiment snapshots.
blueprints.audience: Engineers, researchers, educators and product teams exploring simulation workflows.
blueprints.ux: Scientific workbench: dark instrument-panel visual language, parameter controls, live response charts and experiment archive.
flows: Adjust ambient temperature, heater power, airflow and insulation values.
Run a deterministic local model and inspect peak temperature, settling time and energy estimate.
Compare response curves from two saved runs.
Save a named snapshot with the current parameter set.
blueprints.model: Experiment, ParameterSet, SimulationRun, MetricSeries, Snapshot. Each run stores input assumptions, computed summary metrics and a deterministic trace.
blueprints.guard: The numerical model is illustrative seed logic, not a validated engineering or safety model. Do not use for real design certification, physical control or safety-critical decisions. No external solver or hardware connection.
prompts: Implement a deterministic simulation service that accepts a typed parameter set and returns metrics plus trace points.
Build a responsive chart workspace that overlays saved simulation runs and supports CSV export.
Add experiment persistence, versioned parameter sets and domain tests for model boundaries.

blueprints.name: Hyperplane
blueprints.tagline: Operate a virtual fleet from one clean control surface.
blueprints.purpose: A virtualization console prototype for selecting hosts, inspecting virtual machines, reading resource allocation and exercising safe local VM state transitions.
blueprints.audience: Infrastructure engineers, platform operators and internal IT teams.
blueprints.ux: Light hypervisor fleet console: host rail, VM inventory table, utilization summary and contextual provisioning actions.
flows: Select a host and inspect its allocated CPU, memory and storage.
Search VMs by name, state or operating system.
Start, pause or snapshot a selected VM in local fixture state.
Create a sample VM through a small provisioning dialog.
blueprints.model: Host, VirtualMachine, ResourceAllocation, Image, Snapshot, LifecycleEvent.
blueprints.guard: All hosts and virtual machines are fictional local fixtures. Lifecycle actions update only browser state and never call a hypervisor, cloud provider or host API.
prompts: Define a typed VM lifecycle state machine with guard conditions and domain tests.
Implement host capacity calculations and VM inventory filtering with seeded fixtures.
Create accessible provisioning and snapshot flows with optimistic UI state and rollback handling.

blueprints.name: Remote Relay
blueprints.tagline: A focused workspace for remote sessions and terminal access.
blueprints.purpose: A remote-computing desktop prototype that organizes saved SSH-style profiles, simulated terminal sessions, file-transfer queues and connection audit history.
blueprints.audience: Developers, system administrators, support engineers and remote operations teams.
blueprints.ux: Dark remote operations console: connection sidebar, terminal session canvas, command palette and activity rail.
screens: Session audit history and connection detail
flows: Choose a seeded connection profile and open its simulated terminal.
Run allowlisted demo commands such as pwd, ls, uptime and whoami.
Add a mock file to the transfer queue and inspect its progress state.
Review prior session events and close a session.
blueprints.guard: This prototype never opens network sockets, executes a shell, authenticates to a host or transfers files. The terminal uses canned outputs for allowlisted commands only.
prompts: Implement a typed terminal simulator with an explicit command allowlist and deterministic fixture outputs.
Add session lifecycle, connection profile editing and searchable audit events.
Design a future remote transport adapter boundary without adding live transport in this prototype.

blueprints.name: Vaultline
blueprints.tagline: See pools, volumes, objects and recovery points in one fabric.
blueprints.purpose: A storage administration interface prototype for viewing pool health, managing volume and bucket metadata, browsing object samples and reviewing snapshots.
blueprints.audience: Storage administrators, platform engineers, backup operators and developers working with storage services.
blueprints.ux: Editorial storage fabric console: capacity-first pool cards, volume ledger, object browser and recovery-point timeline.
flows: Inspect pool capacity, allocation and health.
Create a local volume or object bucket with a name and capacity.
Browse seeded objects and inspect metadata.
Create a mock snapshot and review retention entries.
blueprints.model: StoragePool, Volume, Bucket, StoredObject, Snapshot, BackupPolicy, CapacityMetric.
blueprints.guard: No disk, filesystem, NAS, SAN, object-store or backup target is accessed. All operations modify only local mock data; capacity values are illustrative.
prompts: Model pools, volumes, buckets and snapshots with typed constraints and testable capacity calculations.
Build an object browser with metadata filters, breadcrumb navigation and empty states.
Implement a retention timeline and snapshot actions against a local repository adapter.

blueprints.name: Meshwatch
blueprints.tagline: Understand cluster topology, quorum and replica health.
blueprints.purpose: A distributed-systems observability prototype for exploring a seeded cluster topology, node health, leader identity, replica lag and a simulated failover drill.
blueprints.audience: Distributed-systems engineers, SREs, database operators and platform teams.
blueprints.ux: Dark topology map with selectable nodes, quorum indicators, replica state cards and an append-only consensus event log.
screens: Node detail, role and health telemetry
flows: Select a node to inspect role, region, health and replication lag.
Inspect the current leader and quorum membership.
Run a simulated failover drill and update the local leader marker.
Review the generated local event log and reset the fixture.
blueprints.model: Cluster, Node, NodeHealth, Replica, ConsensusTerm, ClusterEvent, FailoverDrill.
blueprints.guard: No distributed consensus, node election, database replication or infrastructure change occurs. The failover action is a visual state simulation only.
prompts: Implement a deterministic cluster-state fixture and a failover reducer with invariant tests.
Build an accessible topology view with keyboard-selectable nodes and a synchronized detail panel.
Add event-log filtering and quorum / replica-health summary calculations.

blueprints.name: Pulsebus
blueprints.tagline: Inspect event streams and consumer health.
blueprints.purpose: A message infrastructure control surface for browsing topics, consumer groups, message payloads, delivery states and publishing synthetic test events.
blueprints.audience: Backend engineers, integration teams, platform operators and event-driven architects.
blueprints.ux: Three-column event bus explorer: topic navigation, live-style message stream and JSON payload inspector/publisher.
screens: Message stream with delivery / retry state
flows: Select a topic and inspect its message stream.
Select a message to inspect headers, schema version and JSON payload.
Validate and publish a synthetic JSON event to the local stream.
Replay a selected sample or inspect the dead-letter queue.
blueprints.model: Topic, ConsumerGroup, Message, MessageHeader, SchemaVersion, DeliveryAttempt, DeadLetterEntry.
blueprints.guard: All events and acknowledgments are local seed data. Publish and replay actions do not connect to Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, Pulsar or any live broker.
prompts: Implement message/topic domain types and an in-memory event repository with publish and replay methods.
Add schema validation, payload inspection and consumer-lag calculations with unit tests.
Create topic filtering, consumer group detail and dead-letter queue review flows.

blueprints.name: Gatehouse
blueprints.tagline: Shape requests as they pass through your middleware stack.
blueprints.purpose: An API gateway and middleware control-plane mockup for browsing routes, configuring policies, inspecting upstream services and reviewing request traces.
blueprints.audience: Backend platform engineers, API architects and integration teams.
blueprints.ux: Dark technical gateway console: route registry, central middleware pipeline visualization, trace ledger and route-policy inspector.
screens: Route registry and upstream service list
Route policy inspector and draft editor
flows: Select a route and inspect its ordered middleware pipeline.
Change the upstream target and timeout in a local policy draft.
Toggle auth, rate-limit, logging and cache layers.
Generate a local test trace and save the route policy draft.
blueprints.model: Route, UpstreamService, MiddlewareLayer, RoutePolicy, RequestTrace, PolicyDraft.
blueprints.guard: No traffic is proxied and no gateway, upstream service or identity provider is contacted. Test traces are synthetic and local only.
prompts: Design a typed route-policy model with ordered middleware layers and policy validation tests.
Build a request trace viewer that correlates route, middleware timing and upstream result fixtures.
Implement route editing and draft persistence behind an adapter interface without live gateway integration.

blueprints.name: Runlevel
blueprints.tagline: Manage process health and runtime compatibility.
blueprints.purpose: A runtime operations console for reviewing hosts and managed processes, comparing language-runtime compatibility, simulating restarts and inspecting rollout history.
blueprints.audience: Platform engineers, SREs, runtime maintainers and application operations teams.
blueprints.ux: Warm editorial operations desk: host selector, process table, runtime compatibility matrix and rollout history tabs.
screens: Runtime host selector and host metrics
Managed process inventory and lifecycle controls
flows: Select a host and inspect CPU, memory and managed processes.
Inspect a process runtime and version.
Request a simulated restart and view local confirmation.
Compare current and target runtime versions and prepare a rollout draft.
blueprints.model: RuntimeHost, RuntimeFamily, RuntimeVersion, ManagedProcess, CompatibilityRule, Rollout, LifecycleEvent.
blueprints.guard: No process is restarted, deployed or upgraded. Host data and compatibility statuses are seeded illustrations, not authoritative runtime compatibility advice.
prompts: Create a runtime compatibility domain model and fixture-driven compatibility matrix.
Implement host selection, process filtering and a simulated process lifecycle reducer.
Add rollout drafts with version comparison, review steps and tests for compatibility warnings.

blueprints.name: The Foundry
blueprints.tagline: Discover the components that make up a software stack.
blueprints.purpose: A curated software-library catalogue for searching libraries and frameworks, inspecting metadata, comparing versions and assembling an illustrative stack manifest.
blueprints.audience: Developers, architects, technical leads and engineering enablement teams.
blueprints.ux: Editorial package atlas: category filters, two-column package cards and a persistent package detail / install-command panel.
screens: Selected package metadata and version history
flows: Filter and search packages by name, family or language.
Select a package and inspect its summary, version and example install command.
Copy the illustrative install command.
Add packages to a local stack comparison.
blueprints.model: Package, PackageVersion, PackageCategory, LanguageTag, RuntimeTarget, StackManifest, StackEntry.
blueprints.guard: Catalogue entries and version numbers are example seed data. No registry metadata is fetched and no package is installed or resolved.
prompts: Define package, version, category and runtime-target schema with seed data and search tests.
Implement a multi-select stack composer and a serializable manifest preview.
Add package version comparison and accessibility improvements to category filters.

blueprints.name: Orbit API Console
blueprints.tagline: Explore an API and shape your first SDK request.
blueprints.purpose: A developer portal prototype with endpoint navigation, parameter editing, local request fixtures, schema examples and JavaScript / Python / Go code snippets.
blueprints.audience: API consumers, SDK developers, integration engineers and platform documentation teams.
blueprints.ux: Developer reference layout: endpoint navigation, central request builder with docs tabs and right-side response inspector.
screens: Try-it request builder and parameter editor
Response inspector and language-specific SDK snippets
flows: Choose an endpoint and inspect method, path and description.
Edit query parameters or a POST request body.
Send a local fixture request and inspect the response JSON.
Switch between JavaScript, Python and Go snippets.
blueprints.model: ApiService, Endpoint, Parameter, RequestSchema, ResponseFixture, CodeSample, ApiVersion.
blueprints.guard: The console does not contact an external API. API base URL and responses are illustrative fixtures; secrets are nonfunctional placeholders.
prompts: Define endpoint, parameter and schema metadata for a small versioned API reference.
Implement a fixture-backed try-it request engine with GET and POST validation tests.
Generate idiomatic JavaScript, Python and Go examples from endpoint metadata.
